prompt: A 400-person organization has uneven interest in Claude Code and little local support capacity. Leadership wants broad adoption without overwhelming the help desk. What rollout plan best addresses the constraint?

options.text: Enable everyone at once and leave all support to the help desk.
Pilot with local champions, then expand with support evidence.
Keep access permanently limited to the first volunteer team.
Use webinar attendance as the only gate for an all-user launch.

feedback.reason: A champion-first staged rollout builds local capability and reveals barriers before increasing support demand.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Adoption is an operating change; feedback and support capacity should inform the rollout sequence.
details.scenarioApplication: A champion-first staged rollout builds local capability and reveals barriers before increasing support demand.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A pilot should be representative enough to surface different workflows, not just the most enthusiastic users.
details.errorCorrection: Distinguish access and activity from demonstrated workflow competence, value, and support readiness.
details.transfer: Scale adoption with measured readiness and support ownership.

messages.text: A simultaneous launch increases support demand before local capability and recurring problems are understood.
Permanent restriction to volunteers prevents the stated broad adoption goal without testing other departments.
Attendance at one webinar does not establish local workflow fit or support readiness.

course.title: Team Enablement and Operational Productivity: Architect Module 5
course.section: M5-S03: Checkpoint: design the team distribution strategy

prompt: Early adopters report strong results, but a later department has different editors, data controls, and review practices. What should the rollout owner do before expanding to that department?

options.text: Copy the first cohort’s setup because the model is unchanged.
Wait for complaints instead of testing the new department.
Validate the new department’s workflow, controls, and setup.
Use installation counts alone to approve departmental expansion.

feedback.reason: A new cohort may have different operating constraints; local discovery and champions reveal them before broad enablement.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Rollout learning should include workflow fit, controls, and support, not only activation counts.
details.scenarioApplication: A new cohort may have different operating constraints; local discovery and champions reveal them before broad enablement.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Reuse the proven baseline where applicable, but validate assumptions that differ by department.
details.errorCorrection: Distinguish access and activity from demonstrated workflow competence, value, and support readiness.
details.transfer: Treat adoption as iterative deployment across people and workflows.

messages.text: The same model does not establish compatible editor integration, data controls, or review practices.
Waiting for requests can leave predictable workflow differences undiscovered until broad exposure.
Installation counts do not show whether the department can complete its work under its controls.

course.title: Team Enablement and Operational Productivity: Architect Module 5
course.section: M5-S03: Checkpoint: design the team distribution strategy

prompt: A pilot has high usage but a growing queue of unresolved questions about safe file editing and test verification. Existing champions cannot handle the current support load, and there is no trained backup. The next broad batch is scheduled tomorrow. What is the most useful adoption decision?

options.text: Expand on schedule because high usage proves readiness.
Cancel the whole program because users asked support questions.
Send feature announcements instead of resolving support gaps.
Narrow expansion; equip champions and verify support readiness.

feedback.reason: Usage alone does not demonstrate that users can operate the workflow safely; the support signal should change the next cohort decision.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A staged rollout can adjust batch size and readiness based on observed support capacity and risk.
details.scenarioApplication: Usage alone does not demonstrate that users can operate the workflow safely; the support signal should change the next cohort decision.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The pilot’s issues may be addressable with focused enablement and verified workflows rather than a permanent stop.
details.errorCorrection: Distinguish access and activity from demonstrated workflow competence, value, and support readiness.
details.transfer: Use adoption and support evidence to set the pace of the next release.

messages.text: Usage shows activity, not safe editing, verification competence, or sufficient support capacity.
Questions identify enablement gaps; they do not by themselves prove the whole program is unsafe.
Feature announcements do not resolve the known editing and verification support needs.

course.title: Team Enablement and Operational Productivity: Architect Module 5
course.section: M5-S03: Checkpoint: design the team distribution strategy

prompt: A team wants to evaluate whether champions are helping adoption. Which measure best distinguishes useful adoption from simple account activation?

options.text: Measure verified work, blockers, and support burden by cohort.
Count enabled accounts as the only adoption success measure.
Use only positive champion survey responses as outcome evidence.
Reward the highest token-consuming cohort as the most productive.

feedback.reason: Activation and usage volume do not show whether users completed suitable work safely or where barriers remain.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A useful rollout measure combines adoption, task outcomes, support burden, and risk indicators.
details.scenarioApplication: Activation and usage volume do not show whether users completed suitable work safely or where barriers remain.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Small cohorts and self-report can be biased; compare to clear baselines and include disconfirming signals.
details.errorCorrection: Distinguish access and activity from demonstrated workflow competence, value, and support readiness.
details.transfer: Measure value and friction in context before expanding or changing the rollout.

messages.text: Activated accounts do not show completed useful work or remaining barriers.
Positive champion surveys omit less-engaged users and disconfirming outcomes.
Higher token use can mean inefficiency; it is not a verified work outcome.

course.title: Team Enablement and Operational Productivity: Architect Module 5
course.section: M5-S03: Checkpoint: design the team distribution strategy

prompt: A pilot’s champions are all experienced CLI engineers, while the next department mostly uses an unfamiliar editor integration. The owner wants evidence for broad expansion into that department. Which pilot adjustment is most useful?

options.text: Keep only expert volunteers and infer results for every editor user.
Include representative editor users and rehearse their real workflow.
Increase the number of CLI experts without changing the tested workflow.
Use token consumption as proof the editor integration works.

feedback.reason: Include users and workflows that represent the next cohort, with its setup, review steps, and support needs. More observations from the original expert group do not test the changed environment.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Include users and workflows that represent the next cohort, with its setup, review steps, and support needs. More observations from the original expert group do not test the changed environment.
details.scenarioApplication: Include users and workflows that represent the next cohort, with its setup, review steps, and support needs. More observations from the original expert group do not test the changed environment.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Reuse validated baseline practices, but gather evidence for materially different users and environments.
details.errorCorrection: Use representative workflow and support evidence for the next scoped rollout decision.
details.transfer: Advance evidenced cohorts while preserving local competence, verification, and escalation.

messages.text: Expert CLI performance does not establish the editor users’ setup and workflow experience.
A larger unrepresentative sample can still omit the relevant integration barriers.
Consumption does not demonstrate installation, safe use, or useful completed work.

course.title: Team Enablement and Operational Productivity: Architect Module 5
course.section: M5-S03: Checkpoint: design the team distribution strategy

prompt: Two departments report more verified completed tasks after introducing champions. They also received different staffing and tooling changes, and no comparison design isolates the champion program. What can the rollout report say?

options.text: Champions caused the entire improvement in both departments.
Report improvement with uncertainty about the champion effect.
The observed task outcomes must be discarded because causality is unknown.
Positive champion surveys establish the exact causal effect.

feedback.reason: Report the observed outcomes and concurrent changes, with limits on attribution. The evidence is useful for learning but does not isolate the effect of champions.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Report the observed outcomes and concurrent changes, with limits on attribution. The evidence is useful for learning but does not isolate the effect of champions.
details.scenarioApplication: Report the observed outcomes and concurrent changes, with limits on attribution. The evidence is useful for learning but does not isolate the effect of champions.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A comparative or staged evaluation can strengthen attribution without withholding routine support.
details.errorCorrection: Use representative workflow and support evidence for the next scoped rollout decision.
details.transfer: Advance evidenced cohorts while preserving local competence, verification, and escalation.

messages.text: Staffing and tooling changes provide competing explanations that this comparison does not separate.
Descriptive outcomes remain useful when their causal limits are disclosed.
Self-report does not isolate the champion program from other changes.

course.title: Team Enablement and Operational Productivity: Architect Module 5
course.section: M5-S03: Checkpoint: design the team distribution strategy

prompt: A departmental cohort has demonstrated its target workflow, passed the stated review and safety checks, and resolved setup blockers. Trained champions and backups can support the measured next batch, and monitoring and escalation are assigned. What rollout action fits?

options.text: Expand the agreed batch with monitoring and retained escalation.
Wait until every possible future workflow has been tested.
Enable the whole organization regardless of department differences.
Remove support and verification because this cohort passed.

feedback.reason: The stated readiness evidence supports the agreed next batch. Preserve support, verification, and monitoring, and reassess before extending beyond the evidenced scope.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The stated readiness evidence supports the agreed next batch. Preserve support, verification, and monitoring, and reassess before extending beyond the evidenced scope.
details.scenarioApplication: The stated readiness evidence supports the agreed next batch. Preserve support, verification, and monitoring, and reassess before extending beyond the evidenced scope.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: New blockers or exceeded support capacity can justify slowing the following batch.
details.errorCorrection: Use representative workflow and support evidence for the next scoped rollout decision.
details.transfer: Advance evidenced cohorts while preserving local competence, verification, and escalation.

messages.text: Unknown future scope is not a prerequisite for the specifically evidenced next batch.
This cohort’s evidence does not establish readiness across every department.
The checks and support are part of what made expansion supportable; passing once does not make them unnecessary.
